meta.name: Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102)
meta.notes: 10 questions across the major AI-102 domains (planning, generative AI, agentic, computer vision, NLP, knowledge mining & document intelligence). Distractors hardened with realistic near-miss services and answer positions rebalanced. | 2026-05-23 keyword-balance pass | 2026-05-25 hardening pass: stripped inline distractor giveaways, rebalanced answer-length distribution | 2026-06-01 +6 questions to unlock learning path

questions.question: You are deploying Azure AI capabilities for an enterprise app and need a single endpoint and key that authorise calls to Vision, Language, Speech and Translator with consolidated billing. Which resource type should you create?
options: One single-service resource created separately for each API you call
An Azure API Management gateway placed in front of four single-service resources
A multi-service Azure AI services resource exposing one shared key
An Azure AI Foundry hub workspace used on its own as the inference endpoint
questions.explanation: A multi-service Azure AI services resource exposes a single endpoint and key that authorise Vision, Language, Speech, Translator and other Azure AI APIs, and rolls all usage onto one bill. Creating one single-service resource per API leaves you managing a separate endpoint and key for every service. An API Management gateway can unify routing in front of those resources, but you still provision, pay for and manage each one — it adds a layer rather than consolidating the service. An Azure AI Foundry hub organises projects, models and connections; it is not the resource that serves the inference APIs.

questions.question: Your team must rotate the access keys on a production Azure AI Language resource without interrupting client traffic that is already in flight. Which sequence is recommended?
options: Regenerate the currently unused key, move all clients to it, then rotate the other
Regenerate both key1 and key2 simultaneously, then redeploy every client application in parallel
Regenerate the key that clients are actively using and let them reconnect to it
Abandon key authentication entirely and switch the resource over to Entra ID tokens
questions.explanation: Azure AI resources expose two keys precisely so you can rotate with zero downtime: regenerate the key no client is currently using, migrate every client to that freshly rotated key, then regenerate the other. Regenerating both keys at once invalidates every live connection until all clients are redeployed, causing an authentication-error window. Regenerating the key clients are actively using breaks their in-flight calls immediately. Switching to Microsoft Entra ID tokens is a valid authentication model, but it replaces key authentication rather than rotating the keys the question asks about.

questions.question: A retailer wants to detect and locate their own product SKUs inside shelf photographs using a small set of labelled images and a no-code training portal. Which Azure service fits best?
options: Azure AI Vision Image Analysis 4.0 using only its built-in generic object tagging
Azure AI Document Intelligence with a custom-trained field-extraction model
Azure AI Video Indexer using a custom-trained brand-and-object model
An Azure AI Custom Vision object-detection project trained on labelled images
questions.explanation: Azure AI Custom Vision lets you upload a small set of labelled images in a no-code portal and train an object-detection model that returns bounding boxes for your own product SKUs. Image Analysis 4.0 recognises only generic objects from Microsoft's prebuilt taxonomy and cannot be trained on labelled images to learn specific SKUs. Document Intelligence extracts fields from forms and documents, not products on a shelf. Video Indexer analyses video timelines and needs video input — it is not a still-image SKU detector even with its custom brand support.

questions.question: The prebuilt invoice model in Azure AI Document Intelligence is missing several vendor-specific fields that your finance team needs extracted automatically. What should you do next?
options: Switch the prebuilt invoice model over to its receipt-extraction variant
Label a few vendor-specific documents and train a custom extraction model
Run the Read OCR model and parse the missing fields with regular expressions
Compose the prebuilt invoice model together with the prebuilt receipt model
questions.explanation: When a prebuilt model omits fields you need, you label a small set of representative documents in Document Intelligence Studio and train a custom extraction model that learns those vendor-specific fields. The prebuilt invoice model has no 'receipt variant' to switch to — invoice and receipt are separate prebuilt models with different schemas and the receipt one extracts merchant/total, not vendor-specific invoice fields. Running Read OCR and regex parsing discards the layout and key-value structure the service already understands, making extraction brittle. Model composition combines several custom models behind one endpoint for routing; it does not add new fields to a prebuilt model.

questions.question: Your chatbot must classify each user utterance into an intent and extract entities such as dates and locations from it. Which Azure AI Language feature should you use?
options: Custom named entity recognition (custom NER) configured on its own
Sentiment analysis with opinion mining enabled on each utterance
Conversational language understanding (CLU) with a trained model
An orchestration workflow that routes utterances to other projects
questions.explanation: Conversational language understanding (CLU), the successor to LUIS, is purpose-built to predict an intent and extract entities from each utterance within a single trained model. Custom NER extracts named entities only and has no concept of intents, so it cannot classify the utterance. Sentiment analysis with opinion mining returns sentiment polarity and aspect-level opinions, not intents. An orchestration workflow connects and routes between CLU, custom question answering and other projects — it relies on an underlying CLU project to do the intent-and-entity work rather than doing it itself.

questions.question: A studio wants Azure to speak marketing copy in a voice that reproduces a specific brand spokesperson, built from professional studio recordings of that person. Which capability is required?
options: Custom Neural Voice trained on the spokesperson's studio recordings
A prebuilt neural voice chosen from the standard text-to-speech catalogue
Personal Voice, the instant zero-shot voice-cloning capability
An SSML voice style-and-role applied to a standard neural voice
questions.explanation: Azure Custom Neural Voice (the Professional tier) trains a synthetic voice from professional studio recordings of a real, consented speaker so it reproduces that spokesperson's identity, and is gated by Microsoft's Limited Access programme to prevent misuse. A prebuilt catalogue voice is a generic, pre-generalised Microsoft speaker and cannot match a named person's specific characteristics. Personal Voice also clones a voice, but it is the zero-shot, consumer-oriented option built from a very short sample — not the studio-trained brand voice described here. SSML voice styles and roles only adjust the expression of an existing voice; they cannot create a new speaker's identity.

questions.question: You want an Azure OpenAI chat deployment to answer questions using your own private PDF policy documents, kept up to date with each release. Which pattern is recommended?
options: Fine-tune the GPT model on the PDF text so it memorises the policy content
Paste the entire text of every policy PDF into the system prompt on each call
Raise the deployment's context window and stream all PDFs in with each request
Index the PDFs in Azure AI Search and query them via the On Your Data feature
questions.explanation: The recommended Retrieval-Augmented Generation pattern is to chunk and embed the PDFs into an Azure AI Search index, then point the Azure OpenAI 'On Your Data' feature at that index so each query retrieves only the relevant passages. Fine-tuning bakes knowledge into the model weights at training time — it teaches style and format rather than fresh facts, and re-running it on every release is slow, costly and still leaves the deployment stale between runs. Pasting every PDF into the system prompt — or simply enlarging the context window to fit them all — burns tokens, raises latency and cost, and still loses accuracy as the document set grows. Only indexed retrieval scales and stays current as policies change.

questions.question: By default, every Azure OpenAI deployment screens prompts and completions for harmful content across categories such as hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content. Which capability provides those built-in filters?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud AI workload threat-protection rules
Azure AI Content Safety filters integrated into the deployment
Azure Policy initiatives scoped to generative AI resources
Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels applied to the model output
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI deployments include Azure AI Content Safety filters by default; they score every prompt and completion for hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content against severity thresholds, and also provide Prompt Shields and protected-material detection. Microsoft Defender for Cloud — including its AI threat-protection plan — monitors deployment-level posture and watches for attacks against the resource, but it does not apply inline content classification to the response stream. Azure Policy enforces how resources are configured, not what text users send. Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels classify and protect data for governance and DLP; they do not moderate harmful content in model traffic.

questions.question: Your assistant must call live external APIs (weather, inventory) during a chat turn and weave the results back into its reply. Which Azure OpenAI capability orchestrates that pattern?
options: Fine-tune the model on transcripts of previous real API responses
Embed the entire API reference documentation into every system prompt
Function (tool) calling, with a tools schema supplied in the request
Switch the deployment to the Assistants API code-interpreter tool
questions.explanation: Function (tool) calling lets the model emit a structured JSON call matching a tools schema you define; your application runs the real weather or inventory API and returns the result, which the model then weaves into its reply. Fine-tuning on past transcripts bakes in stale snapshots and never calls a live API. Embedding API reference docs in the prompt only describes the APIs — it cannot invoke them and wastes tokens. The Assistants API code-interpreter tool runs sandboxed Python for data analysis, not arbitrary external API calls, so it does not orchestrate this pattern.

questions.question: You add a 1,536-dimension embedding produced by Azure OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 to each chunk in an Azure AI Search index so it can be retrieved by vector similarity. How should that field be defined?
options: Collection(Edm.Single) with a dimensions value and a vector profile
Collection(Edm.Double) marked searchable with the standard text analyzer
Edm.String set as both searchable and filterable for similarity queries
A complex field wrapping 1,536 numeric sub-fields, one per dimension
questions.explanation: A vector field in Azure AI Search is typed as Collection(Edm.Single) — a single-precision float array — and must declare a `dimensions` value (1536 here) plus a vector search profile that selects an algorithm such as HNSW. Collection(Edm.Double) is not a valid vector element type and cannot accept a dimensions property; a text analyzer is also meaningless for numeric vectors. Edm.String holds keyword text for full-text search and cannot back vector similarity. A complex type groups named sub-fields for structured objects and cannot be queried as a single embedding vector.

questions.question: An Azure OpenAI chat application is being moved to production. Security requires that no API key be stored in the app, and that calls be authorized by the application's own Azure identity instead. Which approach should you implement?
options: Assign the app a managed identity and grant it the Cognitive Services OpenAI User role, then authenticate with Microsoft Entra tokens
Store key1 in Azure Key Vault and have the app fetch it at startup using a connection string
Embed key2 in an environment variable injected by the deployment pipeline at release time
Place Azure API Management in front of the resource and forward the subscription key on each call
questions.explanation: Granting the app's managed identity the Cognitive Services OpenAI User role and acquiring Microsoft Entra tokens removes keys entirely and authorizes calls by the app's own identity. Fetching key1 from Key Vault still relies on a key — the resource is authenticated by the key, not by the app's identity. Injecting key2 as an environment variable both stores a key and exposes it to anyone who can read the process environment. API Management forwarding a subscription key authorizes the caller to the gateway, not the Azure OpenAI resource by the app's identity, and a key is still in use downstream.

questions.question: A multilingual support team must translate inbound chat messages into English in real time, automatically detecting the source language of each message without it being specified. Which Azure AI service capability handles this?
options: Azure AI Language key phrase extraction run before forwarding the text to a translation step
Azure AI Speech speech translation configured for text-to-text language conversion
Azure AI Translator text translation, which auto-detects the source language when none is supplied
Azure AI Language summarization with the target language set to English on each request
questions.explanation: Azure AI Translator's text translation API detects the source language automatically when the 'from' parameter is omitted and returns the translated text in the requested target language, which fits real-time chat translation. Key phrase extraction surfaces salient terms but performs no translation. Speech translation converts spoken audio, not chat text, so it is the wrong modality. Summarization condenses text and does not translate between languages.

questions.question: A media archive needs to make spoken dialogue in thousands of recorded video files searchable, producing time-stamped transcripts plus detected topics and faces. Which Azure service is purpose-built for this?
options: Azure AI Vision Image Analysis run frame-by-frame on exported video stills
Azure AI Speech batch transcription paired with a separately built search index
Azure AI Video Indexer, which extracts transcripts, topics, faces, and a searchable timeline from video
Azure AI Document Intelligence Read model applied to subtitle sidecar files
questions.explanation: Azure AI Video Indexer analyzes audio and video together to produce time-stamped transcripts, topic detection, face detection, and a searchable index across many files — exactly the archive scenario. Image Analysis on exported stills loses the audio track entirely and cannot transcribe dialogue. Speech batch transcription returns text but no video-level insights such as faces or topics, requiring you to rebuild everything Video Indexer already provides. The Document Intelligence Read model performs OCR on documents and depends on subtitle files that may not exist.

questions.question: You build an Azure AI Search index over support PDFs and want each document enriched with key phrases and detected language as it is ingested, with no custom code. Which Azure AI Search component performs this enrichment during indexing?
options: A scoring profile that boosts documents containing the extracted key phrases at query time
A skillset of built-in cognitive skills attached to the indexer to enrich documents during ingestion
A synonym map that expands query terms to the language variants found in the documents
A semantic ranker configuration applied to the index to reorder results by relevance
questions.explanation: A skillset composed of built-in cognitive skills (key phrase extraction, language detection, OCR, entity recognition) runs inside the indexer pipeline and writes enriched fields with no custom code. A scoring profile only adjusts ranking weights at query time and cannot extract key phrases during ingestion. A synonym map expands query terms; it does not enrich documents as they are indexed. The semantic ranker re-orders results at query time and performs no ingestion-time enrichment.

questions.question: A bank's Azure OpenAI assistant must never reveal another customer's data even if a user crafts an input designed to override the system instructions. Which Azure AI Content Safety capability is designed to detect that class of attack?
options: Protected material detection, which flags known copyrighted text in completions
Groundedness detection, which checks whether a completion is supported by source data
Prompt Shields, which detect jailbreak and indirect prompt-injection attempts in inputs
Severity-based category filters, which score outputs for hate, violence, and self-harm
questions.explanation: Prompt Shields in Azure AI Content Safety are built to detect jailbreak attacks and indirect prompt-injection attempts that try to override system instructions, matching the described threat. Protected material detection flags known copyrighted text, not instruction-override attacks. Groundedness detection checks whether a response is supported by provided source data, which addresses hallucination rather than injection. Severity-based category filters score harmful-content categories such as hate and violence, not manipulation of the system prompt.

questions.question: You must extract entities like 'policy number' and 'claim ID' that are specific to your insurer's documents and do not exist in the prebuilt entity categories of Azure AI Language. Which feature should you use?
options: Prebuilt named entity recognition (NER) filtered to the Quantity and Number categories
Personally identifiable information (PII) detection with the redaction option enabled
Entity linking, which associates recognized entities with Wikipedia knowledge-base IDs
Custom named entity recognition (custom NER) trained on your labelled documents
questions.explanation: Custom NER lets you label your own documents and train a model to extract domain-specific entities such as policy number and claim ID that prebuilt categories do not cover. Prebuilt NER recognizes only Microsoft's fixed category set and cannot learn insurer-specific fields by filtering to Quantity or Number. PII detection finds and can redact personal data types, not arbitrary custom business entities. Entity linking disambiguates recognized entities against a public knowledge base and does not extract new custom entity types.
